steps.text: Write the "Architecture overview" section of the Wikipedia article on 5G network slicing: describe a general network slicing architecture, its layers and the role of the network slice controller.

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Overview
  - different network slice architecture proposals; possible to define general, unified framework mapping common elements
  - two main blocks: slice implementation; slice management and configuration
  - first block: multi-tier, three layers (service layer, network function layer, infrastructure layer), each with distinct tasks in slice definition and deployment
  - second block: centralized network entity, "network slice controller", monitors/manages functionalities between the three layers, coordinates coexistence of multiple slices

## Service layer
- interfaces directly with network business entities (e.g. MVNOs, 3rd party service providers) sharing the physical network
- unified vision of service requirements
- each service = service instance, network characteristics as SLA requirements, satisfied by suitable slice creation

## Network function layer
- creates each network slice from service instance requests from upper layer
- set of network functions with well-defined behaviors and interfaces
- functions placed over virtual network infrastructure, chained -> end-to-end network slice instance
- configuration via network operations managing full lifecycle (placement at slice creation -> de-allocation when no longer needed)
- sharing one network function between slices: better resource efficiency, more complex operations management
- one-to-one mapping function/slice: easier configuration, poor and inefficient resource usage

## Infrastructure layer
- actual physical network topology (radio access network, transport network, core network); every slice multiplexed on it
- provides physical resources to host the network functions of each slice
- heterogeneous components: data centers (storage and computation), routers (networking), base stations (radio bandwidth)

## Network slice controller
- network orchestrator; interfaces with functionalities of each layer to manage each slice request
- benefit: efficient, flexible slice creation, reconfigurable during life-cycle
- tasks:
  - end-to-end service management: map service instances (SLA requirements) to suitable network functions
  - virtual resources definition: virtualize physical resources to simplify allocating network functions
  - slice life-cycle management: monitor performance across three layers, reconfigure for SLA requirement changes
- may be composed of multiple orchestrators, each managing a subset of functionalities per layer
- orchestrators coordinate by exchanging high-level information on state of slice creation and deployment operations

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
There are different proposals for network slice architectures, but it is possible to define a general architecture that maps the common elements of each solution into one general and unified framework. At a high level, the network slicing architecture can be seen as made of two main blocks, one for the actual slice implementation and the other for slice management and configuration. The first block is a multi-tier architecture with three layers (service layer, network function layer, infrastructure layer), and each layer has its own tasks in defining and deploying the slice. The second block is a centralized network entity, which is generically called the network slice controller, that monitors and manages the functionalities between the three layers so that multiple slices can coexist and be coordinated efficiently.

## Service layer

The service layer interfaces directly with the network business entities (e.g. MVNOs and 3rd party service providers) that share the physical network underneath, and it gives a unified vision of the service requirements. Each service is represented formally as a service instance, which contains all the network characteristics as SLA requirements, and these are expected to be fully satisfied when a suitable slice is created.

## Network function layer

The network function layer creates each network slice based on the service instance requests that come from the layer above. It is made of a set of network functions which have well-defined behaviors and interfaces. Multiple network functions are placed over the virtual network infrastructure and they are chained together to create an end-to-end network slice instance that reflects the network characteristics the service asked for. The network functions are configured with a set of network operations that manage their full lifecycle (from when they are placed when a slice is created to when they are de-allocated because the function is not needed anymore).

The same network function can be shared at the same time by different slices to use resources more efficiently, but this makes managing the operations more complex. On the other hand, a one-to-one mapping between each network function and each slice makes configuration easier, but resource usage can be poor and inefficient.

## Infrastructure layer
- actual physical network topology (radio access network, transport network, core network); every slice multiplexed on it
- provides physical resources to host the network functions of each slice
- heterogeneous components: data centers (storage and computation), routers (networking), base stations (radio bandwidth)

## Network slice controller
- network orchestrator; interfaces with functionalities of each layer to manage each slice request
- benefit: efficient, flexible slice creation, reconfigurable during life-cycle
- tasks:
  - end-to-end service management: map service instances (SLA requirements) to suitable network functions
  - virtual resources definition: virtualize physical resources to simplify allocating network functions
  - slice life-cycle management: monitor performance across three layers, reconfigure for SLA requirement changes
- may be composed of multiple orchestrators, each managing a subset of functionalities per layer
- orchestrators coordinate by exchanging high-level information on state of slice creation and deployment operations

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
There are different proposals for network slice architectures, but it is possible to define a general architecture that maps the common elements of each solution into one general and unified framework. At a high level, the network slicing architecture can be seen as made of two main blocks, one for the actual slice implementation and the other for slice management and configuration. The first block is a multi-tier architecture with three layers (service layer, network function layer, infrastructure layer), and each layer has its own tasks in defining and deploying the slice. The second block is a centralized network entity, which is generically called the network slice controller, that monitors and manages the functionalities between the three layers so that multiple slices can coexist and be coordinated efficiently.

## Service layer

The service layer interfaces directly with the network business entities (e.g. MVNOs and 3rd party service providers) that share the physical network underneath, and it gives a unified vision of the service requirements. Each service is represented formally as a service instance, which contains all the network characteristics as SLA requirements, and these are expected to be fully satisfied when a suitable slice is created.

## Network function layer

The network function layer creates each network slice based on the service instance requests that come from the layer above. It is made of a set of network functions which have well-defined behaviors and interfaces. Multiple network functions are placed over the virtual network infrastructure and they are chained together to create an end-to-end network slice instance that reflects the network characteristics the service asked for. The network functions are configured with a set of network operations that manage their full lifecycle (from when they are placed when a slice is created to when they are de-allocated because the function is not needed anymore).

The same network function can be shared at the same time by different slices to use resources more efficiently, but this makes managing the operations more complex. On the other hand, a one-to-one mapping between each network function and each slice makes configuration easier, but resource usage can be poor and inefficient.

## Infrastructure layer

The infrastructure layer is the actual physical network topology (radio access network, transport network and core network) that every network slice is multiplexed on, and it provides the physical network resources that host the network functions making up each slice.

The network domain of the available resources has a heterogeneous set of infrastructure components like data centers (storage and computation capacity resources) and devices for network connectivity such as routers (networking resources) and base stations (radio bandwidth resources).

## Network slice controller

The network slice controller is a network orchestrator. It interfaces with the different functionalities of each layer so that each slice request is managed coherently. The benefit of this network element is that slice creation is efficient and flexible and the slice can be reconfigured during its life-cycle. In practice the network slice controller handles several tasks that give better coordination between the layers:

End-to-end service management: mapping the service instances, which are expressed as SLA requirements, to suitable network functions that can satisfy the service constraints.

Virtual resources definition: virtualizing the physical network resources so that the resource management operations for allocating network functions are simpler.

Slice life-cycle management: monitoring slice performance across all three layers so each slice can be dynamically reconfigured if the SLA requirements change.

The tasks are complex and have different purposes, so the network slice controller can be made of multiple orchestrators that each manage a subset of functionalities of each layer independently. To meet the service requirements, the orchestration entities have to coordinate with each other by exchanging high-level information about the state of the operations in slice creation and deployment.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Although there are different proposals for network slice architectures,[1,2,3] it is possible to define a general architecture that maps the common elements of each solution into a general and unified framework. From a high-level perspective, the network slicing architecture can be considered as composed of two main blocks, one dedicated to the actual slice implementation and the other to slice management and configuration.[4] The first block is designed as a multi-tier architecture composed of three layers (service layer, network function layer, infrastructure layer), each of which contributes to the slice definition and deployment with distinct tasks. The second block is designed as a centralized network entity, generically called the network slice controller, which monitors and manages the functionalities between the three layers in order to efficiently coordinate the coexistence of multiple slices.[5]

## Service layer

The service layer interfaces directly with the network business entities (e.g. MVNOs and 3rd party service providers) that share the underlying physical network, and it provides a unified vision of the service requirements. Each service is formally represented as a service instance, which embeds all the network characteristics in the form of SLA requirements that are expected to be fully satisfied by a suitable slice creation.[1]

## Network function layer

The network function layer is in charge of creating each network slice according to the service instance requests coming from the upper layer. It is composed of a set of network functions that embody well-defined behaviors and interfaces. Multiple network functions are placed over the virtual network infrastructure and chained together to create an end-to-end network slice instance that reflects the network characteristics requested by the service.[6,7] The network functions are configured by means of a set of network operations that allow management of their full lifecycle (from their placement when a slice is created to their de-allocation when the function they provide is no longer needed).[4]

To increase resource usage efficiency, the same network function can be shared simultaneously by different slices, at the cost of more complex operations management. Conversely, a one-to-one mapping between each network function and each slice eases the configuration procedures, but can lead to poor and inefficient resource usage.[6,8]

## Infrastructure layer

The infrastructure layer represents the actual physical network topology (radio access network, transport network and core network) upon which every network slice is multiplexed, and it provides the physical network resources to host the network functions composing each slice.[9]

The network domain of the available resources includes a heterogeneous set of infrastructure components such as data centers (storage and computation capacity resources) and devices enabling network connectivity, such as routers (networking resources) and base stations (radio bandwidth resources).[10]

## Network slice controller

The network slice controller is defined as a network orchestrator that interfaces with the various functionalities performed by each layer in order to coherently manage each slice request. The benefit of such a network element is that it enables efficient and flexible slice creation that can be reconfigured during the slice's life-cycle.[7] Operationally, the network slice controller oversees several tasks that provide more effective coordination between the layers:[11,4,5]

End-to-end service management: mapping of the various service instances, expressed in terms of SLA requirements, to suitable network functions capable of satisfying the service constraints.

Virtual resources definition: virtualization of the physical network resources in order to simplify the resource management operations performed to allocate network functions.

Slice life-cycle management: monitoring of slice performance across all three layers in order to dynamically reconfigure each slice to accommodate possible modifications of the SLA requirements.

Because of the complexity of these tasks, which address different purposes, the network slice controller can be composed of multiple orchestrators that independently manage a subset of the functionalities of each layer. To fulfill the service requirements, the various orchestration entities need to coordinate with each other by exchanging high-level information about the state of the operations involved in slice creation and deployment.[8]
